instructions: Peel the potatoes and slice them into rounds about 1/2 inch thick. Finely chop the onion and the garlic. Chop the parsley leaves. That should be about 1 cup.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic and half of the parsley and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 1 minute.

Add the potatoes, the broth and the salt. The broth should just cover the potatoes. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 20 minutes, until a knife slides through a slice easily.
Add the peas and cook for 3 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the rest of the parsley.
Serve in shallow bowls with the broth spooned over.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Directo al Paladar's classic is the lead: onion, garlic and parsley sautéed, a splash of white wine, potatoes simmered in stock, peas at the end. It uses fish stock and fish crumbs, so this swaps in vegetable broth and leaves the fish out to keep it vegan. The sources slice the potatoes thicker and simmer 25 to 35 minutes; thinner rounds finish in 20. The dried red chili is left out to keep the base mild. The page shows 71 ratings but no average, so this is a fallback lead.
